newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN EXOTICS - Regionals weak and weary.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS - Regionals weak and weary.

text.p: * Malaysian ringgit recovers from 33-month low on talk of Bank Negara intervention overnight. Seen vulnerable to more weakness.
* Indonesian rupiah shows muted reaction to comments by central bank governor, firms partly on expectations of tighter liquidity due to tax payments.
* Thai baht subdued as market loses interest after confirmed central bank intervention on Monday.
* Philippine peso remains under pressure.
* Singapore dollar still weak but sluggish.
Southeast Asian currencies continued to be afflicted by poor sentiment on Tuesday as comments from central bankers and government officials sent mixed signals to the market.

In Malaysia, the ringgit regained some poise on talk Bank Negara had intervened in offshore markets overnight and possibly early on Tuesday, after the currency slid to a 33-month low of 2.5700 against the U.S. dollar.
Dealers said speculative funds sold the ringgit down to its lowest level since October 1994 after Finance Minister Anwar Ibrahim said on Monday the ringgit was still within a "reasonable range".
"There's speculation that Negara was in at the 2.5700 top through agents in Sydney time, as well as in London and New York," said a senior dealer at a European bank in Singapore.
He said U.S. funds were likely to now push the currency towards 2.6000 to the dollar, although the rise could slow as the market was already long of dollars.
Comments by Anwar on Tuesday that Malaysia would allow the exchange rate to be determined by market forces were expected to weigh further on the ringgit, dealers said.
"Buying of dollar/ringgit is still very strong. Immediate target is 2.58. If it rebounds from there, it could go back below 2.53," another European bank dealer said.
The ringgit was at 2.5565/95 to the dollar at 0350 GMT against 2.5310/30 at its close in Kuala Lumpur on Monday.
Indonesian central bank governor Sudradjad Djiwandono's comments that he saw more scope for interest rate cuts if inflation fell, had a muted effect on the rupiah, dealers said.
"The market is moving more in response to the liquidity situation, which is a bit tight because some tax payments are due," a Singapore-based dealer said.
"At the moment, the rupiah is the only currency being spared by speculators. But once speculation in the ringgit has subsided, they will look towards the rupiah," he added.
He said there was a line-up of corporate orders for the dollar below 2,440 but rumours that state banks were looking to sell aggressively above 2,460 were limiting rupiah weakness.
Spot rupiah was at 2,446.0/49.0 at 0350 GMT against an opening 2,450/55.
The Thai baht had a subdued morning, largely due to a lack of interest after the Bank of Thailand (BOT) confirmed it had intervened to support the currency on Monday.
The BOT said the baht had fallen about 15 percent since it switched to a managed float on July 2 from the previous system of pegging the baht to a basket of currencies.
"The speculators got what they wanted with the de facto devaluation. And there are a lot of stale longs in the system putting a cap on the dollar/baht above 30," a Singapore dealer said.
But he said the dollar would be bought on any dips as Thailand's financial woes had not ended.
The baht was quoted at 29.920/29.970 to the dollar in domestic markets at 0350 GMT and at 29.850/950 offshore.
The Singapore dollar, which suffered a knock-on effect from the region's woes on Monday, returned to a more sluggish mode on Tuesday, dealers said.

"There are rumours the central bank was checking rates at the 1.4450 level so the market is wary of any intervention. But it looks like they're just monitoring and haven't shown any physical presence so far," a dealer said.
He added, however, that the authorities were likely to be comfortable with some weakness in the currency, especially in view of the U.S. dollar's steep climb against the mark in recent days.
The Philippine peso recovered some ground but remained weak on the second trading day after its effective devaluation.
The peso was quoted at 29.000/30.000 at 0350 GMT against an opening at around 30 to the dollar.

-- Syed Azman in Kuala Lumpur (603-206 2323), Mantik Kusjanto in Jakarta (6221 384-6364), Anuchit Nguyen in Bangkok (662) 652-0642, Lilian Karunungan in Manila (632-841-8937) and Sonali Desai in Singapore (65-8703090)
